newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - September 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - September 28.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for Reuters by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi. Tel:3326806, 3326813, 3326849 Fax:+91-11-3351006 E-mail:
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Times Of India
TALIBANS CAPTURE KABUL, INDIA CLOSES MISSION

The Afghan capital fell to Pakistan-backed Talebans who after gaining control executed former president Najjibullah and set up an interim Islamic government. President Burhanuddin Rabbani and Prime Minister Gulbaddin Hkmatyaar fled to escape. Najjibullah, 50, who had taken shelter at the UN office in Kabul since April 1992 when the rebels ousted his soviet-backed government after a 14-year war, was dragged to the street and hanged from a lamp-post in the heart of the city. Najjibullah's brother Shahpur Ahmedi, too suffered the same fate. Meanwhile, India closed its deplomatic mission in Kabul and watched the developments without committing any steps.
Financial Express
FOREIGN INVESTORS MAY GET ACCESS TO GOVERNMENT BONDS

The government may soon allow full convertibility of rupee on the capital account. The government is also considering demands to throw open government bonds along with other bonds to foreign investors, said Finance Minister P. Chidambaram. On his way to the annual World Bank meeting in Washington, the minister told foreign investors and non-resident Indian businessmen that decisions on opening the insurance sector to multinational and foreign companies was likely to be taken by March next year.
INDUSTRY MINISTER'S PROPOSAL ON COAL, LIGNITE SHOT DOWN

The Industry Minister's proposal to open the coal and lignite sector to multinational companies (MNCs) was shot down by the Coal Ministry. In the hope of attracting more foreign direct investment, the Industry Ministry had wanted provisions in the amended Mines (nationalisation) Act changed to allow private sector entry in coal mining and development. To this, the Coal Ministry objected, questioning legal validity of allotting captive mining blocks to private parties and opening the sector to MNCs.
BOURSE REGULATOR'S MOVE TO CURB VOLATILITY OF SCRIPS

The bourse regulator has decided on 25 percent weekly price band for restraining the volatility of scrips quoted above par. This forms part of a multi-pronged strategy to improve the vigilance systems of the bourses to check default and illegal transactions by brokers. The bourse regulator also recommends on-line segregation of client and broker transactions, keeping records of brokers and setting up of clearing corporations by stock exchanges. Other suggestions include introduction of a stock-watch mechanism, daily reporting to the bourse regulator on price and volume fluctuations in scrips.
CUSTODIAL SERVICES TO BE SET UP FOR GOVERNMENT PAPERS

The Securities Trading Corp of India (STCI) is set to enter into custodial services exclusively for government securities to widen its role in government bond trading. The custodial services is expected to be operational by fiscal 1997/98, said STCI. This would be a unique product as no other institution is providing such a facility, sources said. The services would enable STCI to create a retail market for government scrips.
The Economic Times
TRADING OF UNLISTED SCRIPS RECOMMENDED ON OTC EXCHANGE

The Dave Committee, set up by the bourse regulator to review working of Over The Counter Exchange of India (OTCEI), has come up with suggestions to help recover the fledgling exchange. It has recommended trading in unlisted scrips as an initial step to add life to OTCEI. The committee pulled up OTCEI's promoters, the financial institutions, for not supporting OTCEI. It suggested, among others, improving management structure, manpower and infrastructure within OTCEI.
BHARAT PETROLEUM TO DEFER 4.5 BLN RUPEE ISSUE

The sluggish primary market took a further dip with Bharat Petroleum Corp Limited (BPCL) deciding to defer its 4.5 billion rupee maiden public issue. The BPCL board plans to come up with the issue once the market situation improved. This is despite the fact that the issue was fully underwritten. The issue was expected to hit the market this October.
Business Standard
BOMBAY BOURSE INDEX DIPS 52.3 POINTS

The Bombay bourse index fell below the 3,300-mark to close at 3,254.73 points, representing a drop of 52.32 points. Friday was the last day of the current settlement cycle. The sharp fall was attributed to sustained bear pressure and lack of support from foreign institutional investors. The market sentiment was largely subdued under the shadow of continuing political uncertainty following charges against former prime minister Narasimha Rao in the St Kitts case. The national index also dropped by 18.18 points to 1,459.42.
POWER DEALS DURING CONGRESS REGIME TO BE INVESTIGATED

The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) has started looking into various contracts awarded in the power sector during the tenure of the Narasimha Rao government. The CBI has written a number of letters to the Power Ministry seeking information on these contracts. Most of the contracts concern the National Thermal Power Corp, the National Hydroelectric Power Corp, the Delhi Electricity Supply Undertaking and the Power Grid Corp of India.
UNIT TRUST'S ROLE IN RELIANCE PRIVATE PLACEMENT SLAMMED

Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI), the bourse regulator, castigated the Unit Trust of India (UTI) for its role in the private placement of the shares of Reliance Industries. The bourse regulator's audit report virtually slammed the door on UTI, saying the 10 billion rupee deal violated all basic investment norms. Among other things, the audit report highlighted that UTI ignored objections raised by Industrial Credit and Investment Corporation of India in the entire deal and even violated the mutual fund norms detailed by the bourse regulator.
SHARP DECLINE IN STEEL DEMAND

Steel producers led by the Steel Authority of India (SAIL) are facing a major glut because of a dip in demand of steel in the second quarter of this year. Production of leading steel producers like TISCO, Rashtriya Ispat Nigam and smaller steel producers like Lloyds Steel have been far lower than projected for the June to September period. The slowdown led to a growing inventory with primary steel producers. Between April and August 1996, the inventory with the primary producers went by 418,000 tonnes from 757,000 tonnes as on April 1, 1996.
COGENTRIX POWER PROJECT CLEARED

The government has cleared the controversial Mangalore Power project. The project is promoted by Cogentrix Inc of the United States and China's Light & Power International. The clearance was accorded after Cogentrix refused to enter into further renegotiations on issues concerning its cost structure and asked the government take a quick decision on the matter. The project will now be placed before the cabinet for extending counter-guarantee.
The Observer
ICICI MUTUAL FUND SCHEMES REPORT HUGE LOSS

The Industrial Credit and Investment Corp of India (ICICI)'s mutual fund schemes, ICICI Premier and ICICI Power, reported huge losses during fiscal 1995/96 (April-March). The revenue account of ICICI premier, the first mutual fund scheme from the ICICI stable, showed a deficit of 394 million rupees. ICICI's other scheme, ICICI power reported a deficit of 129 million rupees during this period. The two schemes incurred a total loss of 524 million rupees in 1995-96.
Business Line
PANEL TO MODIFY TAKEOVER NORMS

The P.N. Bhagwati Committee on takeovers is set to modify some of the proposed regulations. The committee plans to modify regulations on the provision of a escrow account by a corporate raider and on the consolidation of holdings by promoters through preferential offers. Sources said the committee, which has received several suggestions from the industry and merchant bankers, would finalise its report on Sunday, after which the bourse regulator, Securities and Exchange Board of India, would have to approve it.
